{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales_df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float, handling commas
sales_df['revenue'] = sales_df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Check the revenue column after conversion
print("Revenue column type after conversion:", sales_df['revenue'].dtype)
print("Sample revenue values after conversion:", sales_df['revenue'].head(10).tolist())

# Confirm that 'completed' status is what we want for revenue
completed_orders = sales_df[sales_df['status'] == 'completed']
print("Number of completed orders:", len(completed_orders))

# Check for test orders — the brief says to exclude internal test orders
# Since the data dictionary doesn't define 'test orders', and no column indicates test status,
# we must assume that 'test orders' are not labeled.
# But the brief says 'exclude internal test orders' — so we must assume they exist in the data.
# Let's inspect the data to see if there is any clue.

# Look for orders with zero revenue — could be test orders?
zero_revenue_orders = sales_df[sales_df['revenue'] == 0]
print("Number of orders with zero revenue:", len(zero_revenue_orders))

# Check if zero-revenue orders are all completed
zero_revenue_completed = zero_revenue_orders[zero_revenue_orders['status'] == 'completed']
print("Zero-revenue completed orders:", len(zero_revenue_completed))

# Check if any completed orders have zero revenue
completed_zero_revenue = completed_orders[completed_orders['revenue'] == 0]
print("Completed orders with zero revenue:", len(completed_zero_revenue))"}
